name: How can I make a small bathroom feel bigger without moving walls?

mainEntity.name: How can I make a small bathroom feel bigger without moving walls?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You can make a small bathroom feel larger by using light colors, larger tiles, a frameless glass shower, wall‑mounted storage, and good lighting. Smart layout tweaks and visual tricks often matter more than square footage.

Small baths suffer most from clutter, dark corners, and visual breaks. Reducing visual barriers and maximizing vertical space creates a more open feel.

KEY FACTORS:
- Light, cohesive color palette on walls and tile
- Frameless or low‑profile glass instead of a shower curtain
- Floating vanities and recessed storage niches
- Layered lighting (ceiling, vanity, and shower)

Ask your designer or contractor for storage solutions built into walls—like niches and medicine cabinets—to get bulky items off counters. Even in a tight LA condo or bungalow bath, these changes can dramatically improve how the room feels day to day.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use light colors, larger tiles, frameless glass, wall‑mounted or floating storage, and layered lighting to make a small bathroom feel bigger. Visual openness and smart storage often matter more than adding actual square footage.
